label: Classic — Zone System (full tonal scale)
brief: Ansel Adams' Zone System, adapted to a digital edit (Adams, The Negative, 1981; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zone_System). Tone first, colour as shot. 1. Decide which shadow must keep detail and place it in Zone III (L* about 22-33); place the important textured highlight (snow, white stone, bright cloud, skin highlight) in Zone VII-VIII (L* about 68-90); middle grey is Zone V (L* about 44-56). perceptual.zones in each pass is the share of the frame in each of the 11 zones, 0 to X. 2. Expand or contract the scale with contrast, whites, blacks and the tone curve, so the photo runs from a true black (Zone 0-I, a small area) to a near white (Zone IX) with texture, unless the subject is deliberately low or high key. 3. Then dodge and burn locally with lr_create_mask (subject, sky, background): burn a bright sky down about one zone, lift the subject about half a zone, so the eye goes where the photo needs it. Do not trade highlight detail for brightness: the clipping limits still hold.
convergence_hints: stop when the important shadow holds detail in Zone III and the textured highlight sits in Zone VII-VIII
stop when the scale runs from a small true black to a near white and local dodging and burning lead the eye

checks.why: full scale: the darkest 5% of the frame reach Zone II or below
full scale: the brightest 5% of the frame reach Zone VIII or above
